@copilot Repurpose this existing PR directly to make Jetty 9 application request callbacks use captured caller context in both library and javaagent instrumentation. This intentionally supersedes the original requirement that delegated-send preparation observe CLIENT context, including earlier comments preserving that requirement. Request-generation and response-consumption application callbacks should follow the same caller-context policy. The outgoing span may still encompass their elapsed time; span lifetime does not require making that span current in application code.

The existing shared helper instrumentation/jetty-httpclient/jetty-httpclient-9.2/library/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/jetty/httpclient/v9_2/internal/JettyClientTracingListener.java calls wrapRequestListeners(existingListeners, context) with the newly started CLIENT context. Both library and javaagent use this helper, so fixing only the new delegated-send scope is incomplete. Wrap application request listeners with parentContext while retaining the operation context for instrumenter.end and outgoing header injection. Existing response listeners already use the caller context. Inspect supported Jetty request-body generation/content-provider and preparation paths separately: listener wrapping alone does not prove that application code generating the request body runs with the right context. Correct affected application callback boundaries within this Jetty 9 scope. Verify concrete baseline/latest dependency implementations before choosing advice or wrappers.

Reassess the proposed new scope in TracingHttpClient.send() and the existing javaagent scope in JettyHttpClient9Instrumentation. Retain a library-internal operation scope only where justified for propagation/suppression, with explicit caller-context boundaries around application callbacks; do not treat matching the javaagent as sufficient justification. Preserve correct remote server parenting, asynchronous span completion/failure, response-body delivery/backpressure, exception propagation, span-free callers, full custom Context values, and restoration of the caller and any unrelated callback thread context. Independently instrumented outgoing work started by an application request callback should be a sibling of the Jetty CLIENT span, not its child or accidentally suppressed.

Reuse the existing Jetty tests and setup rather than adding a large standalone context test class. Update stale CLIENT-context expectations introduced by this PR and retain compact synchronous exception/no-start behavior coverage where relevant. Cover both library and installed-javaagent request/response callback behavior and actual request-body generation where supported, including inline/asynchronous paths and caller/no-caller cases. Run narrow relevant formatting and tests against supported baseline/latest paths when feasible and report genuine tooling blockers accurately. Keep this to Jetty 9; do not update other PRs or perform the repository-wide audit. #20958 tracks the still-outstanding full audit and must remain open. Acceptance requires the shared library/agent listener fix, investigation and coverage of request-body callback boundaries, justified internal scopes, and preserved remote parentage/lifecycle.

threads.body: [Testing] Both new upload tests use `InputStreamContentProvider`, so they do not exercise the `AsyncContentProvider` listener or the iterator's `Callback`/`Synchronizable` contracts that this proxy must preserve. Jetty uses those contracts to resume deferred uploads, acknowledge chunks, and coordinate iteration; regressions could stall uploads while the current tests still pass. Please add shared library/javaagent integration coverage using a deferred provider, with content offered after `send()`, and verify completion and failure callbacks retain caller context.

replies.body: Added shared library/javaagent integration cases in 77301942 using real DeferredContentProvider uploads offered after send returns. They check received payload, completion, caller context in chunk success and abort-failure callbacks, and request termination.

threads.body: [General] A valid content provider can also implement a public sealed application interface on Java 17+, but copying that interface into the proxy makes `Proxy.newProxyInstance` throw `IllegalArgumentException`. This prevents library requests from reaching `super.send()` and leaves the started CLIENT span without completion listeners in both library and javaagent instrumentation. Restrict proxy interfaces to the Jetty/JDK contracts required for content delivery, traversing application interfaces only to discover those contracts, and add a regression test for a provider with a sealed interface.

replies.body: Fixed in 77301942. Proxy interfaces are now restricted to the supported Jetty/JDK delivery contracts, while hierarchy traversal still discovers inherited contracts. A shared regression sends a typed provider with a public sealed application interface on Java 17+ and verifies request and CLIENT span completion.

@copilot Update this existing PR directly to address the two in-scope findings from Copilot review 5641650176: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20957#pullrequestreview-5641650176. The previous coding attempt is verified finished. Do not create another PR or change other branches.

1. wrapWithContext/addPublicInterfaces currently copies every public application interface from the content provider or iterator into a JDK dynamic proxy. On supported Java 17+ a valid provider may implement an unrelated public sealed application interface; Proxy.newProxyInstance rejects sealed proxy interfaces with IllegalArgumentException. handleRequest has already started the CLIENT span and has not registered completion listeners at this point, so this can fail a library request and leak an agent span. Restrict the implemented proxy interfaces to the actual supported Jetty/JDK contracts needed for content delivery, continuing to traverse inherited application interfaces when necessary to discover those contracts. Do not proxy arbitrary application interfaces or use a Java 17-only production API, since this module must retain its Java 8 compatibility. Preserve optional asynchronous, callback, close, content-type, and synchronization contracts across baseline and latest supported Jetty 9 versions, or use a simpler typed decorator if it preserves all of them. Add focused regression coverage showing that an unrelated application interface, including the sealed-interface failure on a supported modern JDK, cannot break sending or span completion.

2. The newly added body tests use InputStreamContentProvider, which does not exercise deferred upload listener registration or iterator completion/backpressure. Baseline Jetty 9.2.0.v20140526 DeferredContentProvider implements AsyncContentProvider and Closeable; its iterator implements Iterator and Callback, with succeeded/failed forwarding to application chunk callbacks. HttpContent dispatches success/failure based on iterator instanceof Callback. Later supported Jetty 9 versions also use Synchronizable contracts. Add shared library/javaagent integration coverage with a real deferred provider, content offered after send returns, and application success/failure callbacks. Verify payload delivery and request termination, caller Context inside chunk callbacks, span-free callers/custom values, unrelated completion-thread context restoration, and no stalled upload or retained callbacks. Use supported APIs for each tested dependency version and bounded coordination, not sleeps. Keep the coverage focused on these optional contracts rather than enumerating proxy implementation branches.

Preserve all prior request/response callback caller-context behavior, full captured Context, body generation under caller context, removed broad CLIENT send activation, outgoing CLIENT propagation, nested independent operations, and synchronous send error handling. Compile the actual changed main sources and run narrow formatting and shared baseline/library/agent tests when feasible; report environment blockers accurately. #20958 remains open and the full repository audit is not part of this follow-up. Acceptance is that supported custom and deferred providers remain usable in both instrumentation modes and their application callbacks retain caller context without lifecycle or transport regressions.

@copilot Update this existing draft PR #20957 directly for the user's request: "Keep the proxies, remove recursive interface discovery. Let's update the original PR with this so I can compare better." Do not create a new PR or update PR #20959, which intentionally remains a separate javaagent-only boundary-instrumentation alternative.

Keep this PR's proxy-based approach shared by library and javaagent instrumentation and preserve its intended caller-context behavior. In instrumentation/jetty-httpclient/jetty-httpclient-9.2/library/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/instrumentation/jetty/httpclient/v9_2/internal/JettyClientTracingListener.java, replace addSupportedInterfaces and its recursive traversal of implemented interfaces and superclasses with fixed supported interface lists for content providers and iterators. Select supported interfaces with Class.isInstance(target), following the existing pattern in JettyClientWrapUtil. This naturally recognizes inheritance without inspecting application class/interface hierarchies and excludes arbitrary application interfaces, including sealed interfaces.

Preserve the existing allowed provider capabilities: ContentProvider, ContentProvider.Typed, AsyncContentProvider, Synchronizable where available, Callback, and Closeable. Preserve the existing allowed iterator capabilities: Iterator, Synchronizable where available, Callback, and Closeable. Include each interface only when the original target implements it; do not make all proxies implement all capabilities. Use direct class literals for interfaces available at the minimum dependency. Resolve the optional org.eclipse.jetty.client.Synchronizable once during helper initialization in the appropriate library/injected classloader and include it when available; it is absent from the minimum supported Jetty 9.2 version, so do not add a hard dependency on it or repeated per-request lookup. Treat expected ClassNotFoundException as an optional-version probe and do not broadly catch unexpected failures.

Keep provider wrapping and returned-iterator wrapping clear, preferably with separately named entry points or separate fixed lists instead of a boolean that selects both interface discovery and wrapping behavior. A small shared invocation-handler/proxy helper is fine if useful, but avoid unrelated abstractions or refactors. Retain dynamic proxies, captured full caller Context, try-with-resources Scope cleanup, InvocationTargetException unwrapping, the delegate's methods including later-version default methods such as isReproducible, and existing classloader compatibility. Do not replace this with the javaagent boundary-advice design.

Preserve both library and javaagent behavior across the existing Jetty [9.2, 10) range: request listeners and asynchronous request-body generation run under captured caller context, including custom values without a caller span; outgoing propagation still uses the CLIENT span; response consumption and completion retain caller context; original locking, deferred availability notification, chunk success/failure callbacks, and closure remain intact. Do not copy unsupported application interfaces onto proxies or change their instanceof-based capabilities.

Read CONTRIBUTING.md, the knowledge index, and relevant instructions before editing. Reuse the existing shared regression coverage, including sealed application interfaces and deferred providers, and add focused coverage only for concrete gaps such as supported interfaces inherited through a superclass or application subinterface. Run the narrowest relevant spotlessApply directly before behavior validation, then relevant library and installed-javaagent tests against the minimum Jetty 9.2 dependency and a supported recent Jetty 9.x version where feasible. Record exact commands/results or environment blockers in task evidence. Do not wait for CI, weaken behavior to satisfy tests, modify unrelated modules, or reply to or resolve review threads. Preserve this PR's draft state and current branch.
